articles.headline: Price beats Kotaskova to become undisputed champion
keyFacts: Lauren Price defeated Michaela Kotaskova by unanimous decision in Cardiff to become the undisputed world welterweight champion.
Price became the first Welsh fighter to hold all four major world titles, maintaining a perfect record of 11 wins.
Price said more is to come, with talk turning to a potential stadium fight against Claressa Shields next summer.
body: Lauren Price hopes to fight on bigger stages as her career continues [Getty Images] Lauren Price dominated Michaela Kotaskova to seal her place in history by becoming undisputed world welterweight champion.

Price, 32, took an unanimous, shut-out decision and the acclaim of the crowd to add the WBO title to her collection and become the first Welsh fighter to claim the accolade of holding all four major world titles.
Already an Olympic champion and world champion from her amateur days, it further underlined her claim as being among the very best in boxing.
But the way in which she did it, extending a perfect professional record to 11 wins from her 11 fights, suggested there could yet be more to come.
Price v Kotaskova: Watch undisputed title fight after Edwards v McGregor
History, hunger and headline bills - why Price is box office
Edwards' world title aim to join Welsh boxing greats
Price won every round from every judge in front of a partisan Cardiff crowd, producing an unrelenting pace that punished her opponent at every opportunity.
Although Price could not force a stoppage, there was never any doubt she had done enough against an opponent full of stamina and stubbornness.
Kotaskova, beaten only once, but never stopped in her career, showed real heart but had no answer to Price's expertise.
The Tokyo gold medal winner could celebrate even before the final bell sounded, climbing the corner ropes and into the record books.
It was lapped up by a sell-out Utilita Arena crowd who excitedly acknowledged the achievement and the moment.
Wales has produced 14 world champions, some of them genuine greats.
They include, of course, Joe Calzaghe who so often graced this venue with successful defence after successful defence of his super-middleweight crown.
He never reached undisputed status, though he was able to cross the capital city to go from arena to stadium champion.

That is the next challenge for Price, claiming before she left the ring that more is to come while talk immediately turned to five-weight world champion Claressa Shields as a stadium fight next summer.
Champions recognise champions
That is for the future, but this was a night for history - with the calibre of some of the former boxers in the stands a nod to that.
Champions know champions. Five Welsh world title winners were in the capital to watch their compatriot do something never been done before.
From Cinderella Man Steve Robinson and Barry Jones, to the more recent Joe Cordina, who may still be eyeing a stadium return of his own in the coming weeks.
All have been proud to fly the flag, but perhaps none have worn it quite as much on their sleeve - or shorts - as Price has done.
Here, entering to the strains of a Welsh male voice choir, the atmosphere moved from Friday night in a city centre to full-blooded patriotism.
The anthem stirred so much Kotaskova couldn't help but raise an eyebrow before stepping out of her corner.
From then, she had no time to savour the moment let alone consider become an opportunity the Czech Republic's first world champion.
She felt flurries of punches from the first moments and struggled with the unrelenting pace set by the champion.
Steely-eyed, Price refused to allow a breath and, while Kotaskova continued to try and come onto the front foot, she was met by angry, but calculated attacks.
Kotaskova's problems only increased when she was cut in the fifth round, the hooks from the home fighter providing no let up.
At one point in the seventh, Kotaskova took a shot so fierce she almost turned her back to say no more, but still she came and still Price went hunting with hooks.
She could not find the decisive blow, finally letting the tempo slip, and even enjoying the final seconds as she accepted she had done more than enough to win and win a place in boxing history.
Edwards impresses in significant undercard win
Price was not the only Welsh winner on the night as Rhys Edwards secured a significant victory over Lee McGregor, taking an unanimous decision to claim the WBA Continental featherweight championship.
McGregor, 29, had stepped back down to featherweight after two defeats in his last three bouts and had made it clear he knew his chances of returning to world-challenging level was on the line.
His determination to keep coming forward showed what it meant, soaking up several clean shots, but Edwards proved too quick and too sharp.
The 26-year-old from Penygraig also had something to prove after a disappointing draw with Gully Powar last time out.

Then he faded in the latter round, but here Edwards managed to take McGregor's punches and maintain his own pace. It ensured what is perhaps the biggest win of his career, and to leave McGregor contemplating his options.

Elsewhere on the undercard, Willy Gilheaney's unbeaten record was taken away by the experience of Argentinean Alberto Igancio Palmetta, the former Olympic boxer showing plenty of know-how to overcome the Swansea fighter's guts and early control to take an unanimous points win.

Earlier in the night, Doncaster's Jake Goodwin took the decision in a game middleweight bout with Liverpool fighter Sean Arkwright. Goodwin – who had former world featherweight champion Josh Warrington in his corner – had only accepted the fight on two weeks' notice, accepting before he was even granted time off work.
And there were wins for Welsh fighters Brandon Scott and Kane Shepherd, while Cardigan's Josh Mellor and Newport's Lewis Howells fought to a draw.

articles.headline: Georgia commit Marcellus Young Casario honored as younger brother joins Rabun Gap captains
keyFacts: Rabun Gap-Nacoochee football players honored the memory of late teammate Marcellus Young Casario on November 20.
Marcellus Young Casario died November 13 from a sudden medical emergency after committing to play for Georgia.
The player's younger brother, Phoenix, served as an honorary captain for the team's coin toss.
body: For one night, Phoenix Young Casario got to stand where his older brother once belonged .

The younger brother of Marcellus Young Casario joined Rabun Gap-Nacoochee's three captains at midfield Friday night, Nov. 20, serving as an honorary captain for the coin toss as the Georgia football commit's former teammates honored his memory.

Marcellus Young Casario, a defensive lineman at Rabun Gap, died Nov. 13 following a sudden medical emergency, the school confirmed to USA TODAY Sports. He was a three-star recruit from Halifax, Nova Scotia, who had committed to Georgia and was on track to graduate in December before enrolling early with the Bulldogs .

Joining Rabun Gap captains Segun Alexander, Jacob Burns and Jaxon Totherow for tonight’s coin toss as an honorary captain is Marcellus Young Casario’s younger brother, Phoenix. pic.twitter.com/E3K2iqT6wf

— Wesley Branch (@Wesley__Branch) November 21, 2026 Known affectionately as "Mar" by his coaches, friends and teammates, Young Casario spent two years at Rabun Gap and quickly became an important part of the school community.
He was a key contributor for the Eagles this season, recording 12 tackles for loss, 10 sacks and a forced fumble while helping the team finish 7-4.

"He was everything a coach wants in a player," Rabun Gap head coach Derek White said in the school's statement following Young Casario's death. "Mar truly embodied our mission to 'love one another.' He was known for his relentless dedication, and his journey as a student-athlete was marked by hard work and a true brotherhood with his teammates."
The school described Marcellus Young Casario as a natural leader, loyal friend and standout student-athlete who was loved across campus.
"Mar brought light, faith, and character to everything he did, and his absence is a tremendous void in our close-knit community," Head of School Bob Ahrens said.

Friday night's tribute gave Marcellus' younger brother an opportunity to stand alongside the teammates who shared the field with his older brother, ensuring Marcellus remained part of the Rabun Gap football family as the Eagles' postseason run continued.

articles.headline: Fantasy Baseball Offseason Tracker: Royce Lewis provides depth for Dodgers' aging infield
keyFacts: MLB players and teams are completing mid-November signings and trades before an anticipated upcoming lockout halts all transactions.
Analysts Scott White and Chris Towers provided fantasy baseball breakdowns for key offseason moves, including Royce Lewis joining the Dodgers and Maikel Garcia moving to the Mariners.
Several players accepted qualifying offers or signed new contracts, such as David Bednar staying with the Yankees and Sonny Gray joining the Twins.
body: A lockout may be coming, but nobody told the hot stove. It's already burning bright with a series of mid-November signings.

Once the lockout becomes official, the signings -- and all other transactions -- will cease, but those that occur before then will still count toward the date when baseball is allowed to resume. So we'd better document them all here, just like any other offseason, breaking down their impact for Fantasy Baseball.

That's what Scott White and Chris Towers intend to do over the next few weeks, at least, before everything goes quiet. They'll eventually pick up where they left off when the hot stove heats up again in ... March? Hopefully not much later than that.
Whatever the timeline, you'll want this page bookmarked so you can get the first word on everything that happens.
Royce Lewis traded to Dodgers

At first glance, this looks like the nail in the coffin for a player whose Fantasy value has already been in free fall, but Lewis can play all over the diamond and the Dodgers have no shortage of geriatric players. He may not play as consistently as he did with the Twins, but between spelling Max Muncy at third base, spelling Freddie Freeman at first base, and filling in for whatever injury pops up, Lewis should play enough to be of some use in Rotisserie leagues, with their larger lineups.

And that's all you should have been counting on anyway with the way his numbers have trended since 2024. He made such a splash to begin his career that it seemed like only injuries would hold him back, but he's shown himself to be just a .230 hitter over the past three years. Maybe with consistent playing time, he could eke out 20 homers, particularly now that he's in a more favorable venue for him, but again, his playing time is about to be less consistent, not more. --Scott White
Maikel Garcia traded to Mariners

This is a trade that makes a ton of sense for real-life baseball but might be a disaster for Fantasy. The Mariners got -0.5 WAR from their third basemen in 2026, per FanGraphs, and Garcia represents a significant upgrade from that. As recently as 2025, put up a .286/.351/.449 line and was a borderline elite Fantasy option as a result.

Unfortunately for our purposes, this trade makes it a lot less likely he'll live up to that level of play in 2027. Kauffman Stadium in Kansas City suppresses homers but is generally a pretty good offensive environment, sporting the seventh-best park factor for hitters, per BaseballSavant.com. T-Mobile Park in Seattle? It's the worst hitter's park in baseball by a pretty wide margin, though how that impacts each individual hitter often varies. Randy Arozarena more or less held serve in his time in Seattle, while someone like Eugenio Suarez struggled mightily in both stints there. It's something about the way hitters see the ball and how the humid, often chilly atmosphere affects batted balls' trajectories. There just isn't another offensive environment in baseball quite like T-Mobile Park, and it generally serves as a drag on offense across the board.

If Garcia can hit like he did in 2025, he'll still be very fantasy-relevant, however. That season saw Garcia max out his power, bumping his average exit velocity to 91.3 mph, while also increasing his launch angle, allowing him to tap into far more of that power than ever before. That he did it without sacrificing his superlative contact skills made for a very strong package. But he gave back nearly all of those improvements in 2026 and returned to being a roughly average hitter. He struggled while playing through injuries to his left hand and wrist before eventually going on the IL for nearly two months, then struggled with hamstring issues late in the season. If the injuries explain his struggles, then betting on a bounceback makes sense, even in Seattle.

But 2025 might have just been a career year, and the move to T-Mobile Park makes it even less likely he'll get back to that level. Garcia's price has already slipped to 169.4 in early NFBC drafts, but I'd expect it to drop even farther after this. He's a fringe starting-caliber third baseman for Fantasy, and I'd take at least Curtis Mead and Isaac Paredes ahead of him, among players with a current lower ADP. --Chris Towers
Bryce Miller traded to the Royals

While Maikel Garcia is going to the worst hitter's park in the league, Miller suffers from the opposite move, exiting one of the best pitching environments in the league. It's one he has specifically benefited from, sporting a career 3.49 ERA at home compared to a 4.63 ERA on the road. It would be overly simplistic to say he has lost whatever Fantasy relevance he had with this move, but it might not end up wrong.

To add some nuance, I think Miller can be a good pitcher in any offensive environment; he just hasn't been for long. He's had stretches across different seasons where he has looked like an ace, but he never manages to sustain it. He has pitched through various elbow issues over the years, but when he is right, he rides a high-vert, high-velo fastball to very good results. Let's not forget that he started the 2026 season with a 1.71 ERA and 10.6 K/9 in his first eight starts, but then he tried pitching through a lat issue and wasn't the same. Still, it was another reminder of how good he can be at his best. Given the inconsistency and the park downgrade, Miller should continue to see his price fall. He's down to 266.3 in those early NFBC drafts and should probably just be a reserve round dart throw now that he's with the Royals. --Chris Towers
Sonny Gray signs with the Twins

It's not the first place I would have bet on Gray signing, but the Twins have made it clear since the most recent trade deadline that they aren't looking to rebuild. The deal is officially for one year but includes a 2028 player option for the 37-year-old Gray, meaning the Twins will either be happy about getting one great season out of him or will be looking at a fairly onerous (but short!) deal for 2028. It's a tradeoff worth making for a team like the Twins, who have talent in the rotation but little in the way of sure things, either from a performance or a health perspective. Gray is seemingly a different type of pitcher every season, but from a real-life perspective, it's easy to see the appeal in employing him: He has made at least 24 starts in every season since 2017 (minus the shortened 2020 season) and has had an ERA over 4.00 just twice in his past eight seasons.

From a Fantasy perspective, his value is a little less clear. He had an excellent 2026 season that saw him take advantage of an elite Red Sox defense to put up a 2.72 ERA. It did, however, come with a huge decrease in his strikeout rate, and that came after two seasons with a combined ERA of 4.07. He's almost always a must-start pitcher, but it often feels like you can't fully trust him. Of course, with an ADP around 150 in early drafts, it doesn't really matter if you can fully trust him. Just roll him out there, hope the ERA is closer to 3.50 than 4.00 and don't overthink it. He's a nice rotation filler as long as you don't expect him to be an ace. --Chris Towers
David Bednar accepts Yankees' qualifying offer

This one comes as a mild surprise and makes me wonder if Bednar just really wanted to stay with a team that wasn't willing to give him a multi-year commitment. He's a 32-year-old closer, and while he has mostly been a very good one over the past six seasons, there have been enough bumps in the road along the way to make the risk for Bednar pretty obvious. But from a Fantasy perspective, Bednar safely looks like a top-12 closer now that he's returning to the Yankees. His strikeout rate regressed in 2026, but his swinging-strike rate was actually higher than the previous season, and none of his underlying metrics otherwise really tell the story of a pitcher in decline. He's somewhere shy of the elite tier of closers for Fantasy, but he's good enough (and secure enough in his role for a good team) to be worth drafting as your primary source of saves. --Chris Towers
Ryan Jeffers accepts Twins' qualifying offer

It was a mild surprise to see the Twins extend Jeffers the qualifying offer, but it's not a surprise to see him accept it. Jeffers is a solid starting catcher -- good enough to be worth a fair share of playing time from the DH spot but he isn't the kind of player who was likely looking at a bunch of $50-plus million offers either. It's why taking the $23.2 million qualifying offer (and becoming the highest-paid catcher in baseball by annual value!) makes some sense here.

It also keeps the status quo in line for Jeffers. He'll play a decent amount and be reasonably productive when he's out there, but Jeffers' apparent breakout in the first half of 2026 proved unsustainable as he settled in more or less where we've come to expect him to be. He's a good hitter for a catcher, but given the strength of the position, he's more of a solid No. 2 catcher option than a true difference maker. That's nice to have around when it comes at the cost of a pick around 200th overall, as it should in most leagues. --Chris Towers
Dustin May signs with White Sox

There might be some sticker shock here – "$50 million for a career 4.12 ERA pitcher who has never thrown 150 innings in a season?" – but that's just the market rate for pitchers who reach free agency with their arms attached. May has been viewed as someone with a lot of upside over the years, but I think we're past that point after he showed little more than mid-rotation abilities in two seasons split between the Dodgers, Red Sox, and Brewers. He's a nice rotation filler for the White Sox, but unless something drastic happens to change his profile, he's a better source of GIFs than Fantasy production at this point in his career. --Chris Towers
Jake Bauers signs with Red Sox

After a surprise breakthrough season in which the underlying data was as sparkling as the top-line production, the biggest concern for Bauers was whether he'd sign with an organization that would help or hinder his follow-up campaign. By most outward indicators, he chose poorly. Sure, he'll be thrilled to get $58 million over the next four years, but his expected home run number at Fenway Park, with its deep right field fence, was only 18, tied for worst among all 30 venues.

He also joins a crowd of five players for four spots -- that is, unless (or until?) the Red Sox trade Jarren Duran. Even if Bauers himself isn't the one to sacrifice at-bats because of it (and look, he's no sure thing, for as good as he was in 2026), the potential impact on Willson Contreras, Roman Anthony, Wilyer Abreu and Duran makes his arrival a net negative for Fantasy. Bottom line is that this signing only amplifies the natural skepticism for a late-career breakout and explains why Bauers barely ranks inside my top 30 outfielders. --Scott White
Emilio Pagan signs with Tigers

The Tigers weren't willing to pay Kenley Jansen $12 million to be their closer, declining his option at the start of the offseason, and then turned around and signed Pagan for about the same amount. Probably safe to assume, then, he's their new closer after serving in the same capacity for the Reds the past two years. His 2026 performance was solid overall, but he was particularly dominant after returning from an early hamstring injury, delivering a 1.88 ERA, 0.84 WHIP and 10.7 K/9 over his final 30 appearances. The home run issues that prevented him from becoming a closer earlier in his career remain acute. Still, if he was able to navigate the past two years in Cincinnati with them, for as homer-friendly as that environment is, he should be able to do the same in Detroit. He'll be a budget-friendly RP2 on Draft Day. --Scott White
Evan Phillips signs with the Braves

The first multi-year signing of the offseason wasn't a headline name, and Phillips seems likely to open the season as the setup man behind Robert Suarez with his new squad. But Phillips is being paid over $10 million a year on a three-year deal, which is a decent-sized investment for a non-closer and reflects the upside he once showed in a high-leverage role. He came back from his June 2025 Tommy John surgery to pitch effectively for the Dodgers in 2026, posting a 3.46 ERA over 26 innings. While the underlying data isn't quite as promising, he still missed a ton of bats and had good control. The velocity also bounced all the way back and then some, past pre-injury levels.

Assuming the Braves don't bring back Raisel Iglesias, Suarez is locked in as the closer coming off a 1.06 ERA, but seeing as he missed three months of the 2026 season with elbow discomfort, there's a non-zero chance Phillips figures into the ninth-inning situation at some point in 2027. He's not necessarily a name you need to know for Draft Day in most leagues, but Phillips could be very relevant in 2027 if things go sideways for Suarez in the way they so often do for pitchers in their mid-30s. --Chris Towers

articles.headline: The Witcher 4 Gets Official Update on Physical Release
keyFacts: CD Projekt confirmed that The Witcher 4 will receive a physical release in 2028.
Joint CEO Michał Nowakowski stated that the studio wants to offer a box with physical collectibles.
Nowakowski acknowledged uncertainty over whether the game will include a physical disc due to Sony ending disc production.
body: CD Projekt has confirmed that a physical version of The Witcher 4 will be released, even though the RPG is slated to launch after Sony Interactive Entertainment plans to stops producing physical games for PlayStation 5. Whether The Witcher 4 will be released on a physical disc is another matter entirely.
Will The Witcher 4 get a physical release?

Sony plans to end the production of game discs for PlayStation consoles in January 2028. The Witcher 4 is the highest-profile AAA game currently slated to launch that year, and it comes from a studio that enjoys releasing its games physically. In an interview with The Game Business from August, CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski confirmed that CD Projekt would still like to release a physical version of The Witcher 4.

"We’re big fans of people having access to tangible collectible things. We’re nerds ourselves, and we like that. We always supported that," Nowakowski explained. "So, whatever is the case, we’re going to be for sure having a box. We’re going to have a box that’s going to have some feelies in it. Something you’re going to be wanting to open up and enjoy."

That said, Nowakowski said he's unsure whether the game itself will be on a disc, as CD Projekt has no control over what Sony decides to manufacture. "We know what PlayStation has announced. And we have no influence on the policies of the first parties," he admitted. "The discs for the first parties, including PlayStation, have to be manufactured in their own factories. So, if they stop manufacturing indeed by 2028, then yes [we won’t have a disc]."

Although Nowakowski went on to tell The Game Business that he has "no influence" over whether it'll even be possible to print discs for The Witcher 4, it's good that CD Projekt is committing to a physical release regardless. That said, it's clear that PlayStation needs to better explain its plans to developers, some of whom are clearly still expressing demand for physical discs.

The Witcher 4 will be released on PS5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X sometime in 2028. Before then, fans of the series can look forward to a current-generation remaster of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt on Sept. 29 and the Songs of the Past expansion for that game sometime in 2027.

articles.headline: Palisades Fire arsonist found guilty on all counts in deadly blaze that killed 12
keyFacts: A federal jury found Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty on all federal counts for starting the deadly Palisades Fire.
The blaze caused 12 deaths, destroyed 6,837 homes, and burned 23,448 acres, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department.
Rinderknecht faces up to 20 years in federal prison per count, with sentencing scheduled for March 17.
body: The California man accused of starting the Palisades Fire in January 2025 was found guilty on all counts by a federal jury on Friday after his mistrial in June.

Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, faced two federal charges for destruction of property by means of fire and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce. He pleaded not guilty. His sentencing date was scheduled for March 17.

The convicted defendant’s actions resulted in 12 deaths, 6,837 destroyed homes, and 23,448 burned acres last year, according to a count from the Los Angeles Fire Department. Most of the damage was concentrated in the Pacific Palisades, Topanga, and the Malibu shoreline.

Rinderknecht underwent a second federal trial this month after his first trial ended with a deadlocked jury. Ten jurors were in favor of an acquittal. This time, all 12 jurors decided the alleged arsonist was guilty after deliberating for two days.

Prosecutors alleged that Rinderknecht, who worked as an Uber driver at the time, intentionally started a brush fire on Jan. 1, 2025, with a lighter. His DNA matched the DNA found on the lighter. The initial blaze smoldered underground before reigniting as the deadly Palisades Fire six days later.

Among the evidence presented at trial was his ChatGPT history, which shows the suspect asking the OpenAI chatbot whether a person was at fault if their cigarette caused a wildfire . Rinderknecht’s geolocation data from his phone showed he was 30 feet away from the flames as they began to spread.

The defense insisted he did not start the fire despite evidence showing otherwise. Both sides agreed that Rinderknecht called 911 multiple times, but his attorneys argued he was only a witness to the fire.
Regardless of the defense’s case, the defendant was ultimately convicted. Rinderknecht could serve up to 20 years in federal prison for each count. The minimum sentence is five years.
JUDGE DECLARES MISTRIAL IN PALISADES FIRE ARSON CASE AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS
First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California welcomed the jury’s decision.
The jury “came back and they held him accountable for the entire thing because that’s consistent with the evidence,” Essayli said. “We’re happy with this jury. They did the right thing.”

articles.headline: Palmer Luckey wants to build a floating island that can last 1,000 years — Oculus Rift founder says SLAB will work outside of 'state/local laws that cripple critical American industries'
keyFacts: Palmer Luckey revealed plans to develop SLAB, an offshore platform designed to support industrial operations for 1,000 years.
Luckey said the platform aims to lower costs and avoid state and local regulations that constrain American industries.
SLAB remains under development with no publicly confirmed construction schedule, installation location, or detailed engineering specifications.
body: - Palmer Luckey wants a floating industrial island designed to last 1,000 years
- SLAB could accommodate oil refineries, metal processing plants, and desalination facilities
- The proposed offshore platform aims to avoid restrictive American state regulations
Palmer Luckey, the entrepreneur behind Oculus and defense technology company Anduril, has revealed he wants to develop a massive offshore platform designed to support industrial operations.
The proposed project, called SLAB, would provide space for activities including metal production, medical research, water desalination, oil refining, and chemical engineering.
Luckey says the structure could remain operational for 1,000 years, offering American industries an alternative to conventional land-based facilities.
SLAB could accommodate heavy industries without conventional land restrictions
Unlike floating offshore settlements and data centers, SLAB is an industrial installation capable of supporting activities requiring substantial infrastructure and specialized equipment.
Its proposed facilities include metal processing plants, medical research and treatment centers, desalination installations, petroleum refineries, and chemical engineering operations.
These industries frequently require considerable space, expensive infrastructure, and access to resources that can make conventional facility development financially demanding.
Establishing installations offshore could provide another location for such operations while reducing dependence on expensive industrial land and existing municipal arrangements.

The financial argument also forms an important part of the proposal, with offshore construction intended to cost less than acquiring suitable conventional property.
Avoiding certain state and local restrictions is another stated objective, particularly regulations that can constrain industrial activities within established American jurisdictions.
The project's development follows an approach associated with seasteading, which involves establishing permanent or long-term human infrastructure on bodies of water.
However, SLAB differs from many previous proposals because its primary purpose involves industrial production rather than just another sovereign AI territory.
Its design also raises substantial engineering requirements, particularly concerning structural durability and the conditions associated with continuous exposure to seawater.
Concrete construction, offshore maintenance, corrosion affecting associated equipment, and the logistics of supporting industrial operations would all require careful consideration.
SLAB has secured funding
SLAB originated in 2014, following Facebook's acquisition of Oculus, the virtual reality company founded by Luckey.
The acquisition provided financial resources for his various experimental projects, including helicopter flight training and the development of an offshore industrial platform.
Luckey subsequently established the initiative with several associates, who reportedly financed its development at a $1 billion valuation in 2017.
Recent additional funding has also supported the effort, although the amount raised and identities of the latest financial contributors remain undisclosed.
The project also carries an explicitly American industrial ambition, rather than the separation from established national governments associated with some seasteading proposals.
Its stated purpose involves creating additional capacity for domestic industries while providing an alternative to regulations considered restrictive by its financial backers.

“The goal was to be cheaper than land and absent state/local laws that cripple critical American industries like metal processing, medical research/treatment, desalination, oil refining, chemical engineering, and more,” Luckey said.
The proposal has attracted reactions from social media users, with some questioning why American industrial development might need to move offshore in the first place.
An X user suggested that the growing interest in building entire cities at sea reflected serious difficulties associated with conventional land development in the U.S.
Palmer Luckey was also asked how far SLAB would need to sit from the American coastline to avoid falling under US jurisdiction, and his response was “three miles”.
SLAB remains under development, with no publicly confirmed construction schedule, installation location, or detailed engineering specifications.

articles.headline: Sophie Cunningham reveals what qualities she wants in her future husband
keyFacts: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham stated in a Maxim interview that she has high standards for her future husband.
Cunningham said she wants a partner who is Christ-centered, taller than her 6-foot-1 height, athletic, confident, and secure.
Cunningham sparked romance rumors with athletic trainer Frank Adams in August, though neither has publicly addressed the claims.
body: Sophie Cunningham knows what she wants in her next partner.

The Indiana Fever guard made her Maxim debut as she graces the cover of the magazine's November/December issue. The WNBA star shared the cover, which features her in a black-and-white image sporting a black leather jacket that slightly tilts off her shoulder, matching leather pants, as her wavy tresses flow in the air.

In her exclusive interview with the publication, she spoke about big moments in her WNBA career as well as making rare comments about her love life. She shared that she has very specific characteristics that she wants her future husband to possess.
“I have a very high standard for my future husband,” Cunningham said. “He’ll be someone who is Christ-centered and can lead me in my walk with Jesus. Someone who’s friendly, confident, and secure."
She added that, for physical characteristics, she would want to be with "someone who is taller than me."
“I’m already so tall. The last thing I wanna do is bend down to kiss my husband goodnight. No, thanks,” Cunningham said.
The WNBA guard is 6-foot-1 and also wants her partner to be athletic like her.
Cunningham noted that he has to be "just a good human with similar morals and values."
What's essential for Cunningham, who during her WNBA season is waking up in different cities, is someone who can understand how important it is to be confident in themselves.

articles.headline: Can Mauricio Pochettino save Man United from Premier League relegation?
keyFacts: Mauricio Pochettino has replaced Michael Carrick as Manchester United manager after leaving the United States national team.
Manchester United currently sits in the Premier League relegation zone with only one win this season.
Pochettino will take charge of his first match as Manchester United manager against rivals Liverpool.
body: Manchester United will be led by a third manager in three years when Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first match since replacing Michael Carrick.

The fact that the Premier League clash is against their fierce rivals Liverpool – the team that, with United, are joint record English top-flight champions – is an added twist to a sordid recent tale for the Manchester club.
When Sir Alex Ferguson retired after lifting a then-record 20th league title in 2013, the Red Devils had climbed to the biggest and richest club in the world.
Now, apart from not being able to claim a Premier League crown since 2013, they are laden with debt – and worse still, they sit inside the relegation zone.
Can Pochettino save Man United from relegation?

The last time United were relegated from the top flight was in the 1973–1974 season. That came only six years after one of the club’s greatest nights – the lifting of the European Cup (now the Champions League), making them the first English club to do so.
Their fall this time around has not come quite as quickly, with their last crowning as European champions in 2008, and they have not been relegated – yet.

Few expect them to be. It would be unthinkable given the changed landscape of the entire footballing world, which has become awash with finances that clearly separate the elite and their resources from the rest.
When Pochettino was introduced to the media for the first time on Friday, the gathered press did not mention the word “relegation” even once.

So the simple answer is: yes, he can save the club from relegation. The longer equation is that the alternative would surely be the greatest shock in the history of a game famed for upsets and underdogs.
What problem does Pochettino need to solve first at United?
Words like identity, fitness, formation, and one that Pochettino awkwardly dropped on Friday, “philosophy”, have dogged every manager at Old Trafford since Ferguson’s departure.
“We arrived with the idea to create something from scratch, with our own philosophy and how we like to work,” Pochettino told the gathered reporters.
“We need to improve our players, find a way to perform, but the future and identity of the club is very clear.
“It is an historic club with an amazing years competing and being one of the best in the world.
“It is difficult to find another club that is the size of United. We need to be open-minded to do our best, and the players need to buy the idea that we need to improve.
“The job is to get the rest of the historic club, Manchester United, into a different place to where we are now.”
All of that can wait, because Liverpool are the next opponents, and for United, they do not come any bigger.

The Manchester derby has taken on a new level in recent years – although the tide there may also soon turn, depending on City’s appeal against their charges – but the rivalries against the Reds and Leeds United have the deepest roots for United fans.
A recent defeat to the revived latter still weighs heavily.

Pochettino needs to find a way for the team to start winning, and it needs to come soon. The club’s opening to the season is their worst since 1986, and one win – the worst return in the league – has left United just one point off bottom place.
By the time Pochettino and his United players walk out to the hostility of the Anfield crowd, they could be at the very foot of the table.
Will Pochettino change United’s formation?

The easiest part of the equation for Pochettino is the formation. With the United States national team, which he left to join United, the Argentinian deployed the 4-2-3-1 tactic that even Ferguson had evolved to in his final years.
Pochettino’s Tottenham, the club he made his managerial name with, were always set out in the same way with Harry Kane leading the line.

The United squad – which were moved to an uncomfortable 3-4-3 by Carrick’s predecessor, Ruben Amorim – are built for Pochettino’s style, but the task of melding them together had eluded Carrick and will be the key to their imminent return.
What long-term problems does Pochettino face at United?
The off-field troubles at United are well documented. The club are weighed down by the debts accrued with the Glazer family’s 2005 purchase.
Jim Ratcliffe’s investment three years ago has seen the Englishman and his INEOS group take control of footballing matters, but the annual interest the club pays remains a heavy burden.
The ownership is committed to its plan to rebuild the Old Trafford stadium to increase capacity and, with it, move the club to a more sustainable future.

That means the spending power that once saw United lead the way in transfer signings has diminished to the point where they cannot compete financially with Liverpool, City and Arsenal on the domestic front, let alone Spanish giants Real Madrid and Barcelona on the continent.
This is no easy fix for the manager or their owners, and is undoubtedly the long-term challenge for everyone involved.
What signings will Pochettino and United target in January transfer window?
Although the squad is set up for a 4-2-3-1 formation, they lack strength in depth.
Striker Benjamin Sesko has had an injury-plagued start to his United career since his move two seasons ago, and the Serbian international was far from the finished product when he arrived.

The 23-year-old’s absence this season has left a glaring hole up front, with Cameroon forward Bryan Mbeumo admirably leading the line with great endeavour, but lacking the presence a lone striker requires.
Despite needing a world-class finisher and being well stocked at the back, United have problems at the other end of the pitch, shipping 30 goals in all competitions this season.
Only two teams have conceded more than United’s 19 in the Premier League.
Luke Shaw’s availability at left-back has left United exposed in that position and made their failure to sign Lewis Hall in the summer all the more galling.

The Newcastle defender has since shone on international duty for England, and a move for the exciting 22-year-old in January seems the most obvious attempt United must make to appease their hugely unsettled fanbase.
What is Pochettino’s best Premier League finish?
Pochettino’s second-place finish with Tottenham in 2017 remains the North London club’s best league finish since 1962, only two years after their last top-flight title.
Will Pochettino be given enough time by United’s owners?
Pochettino will be the ninth manager to take charge of United in the last 13 seasons, and that does not include a further three interim coaches.
United fans never turn on their manager, and only recently, for the first time in the club’s history, have they turned on the players.
The same clearly cannot be said of the ownership.

It felt that Pochettino corrected his “philosophy” faux pas before he had finished that same answer on Friday. It was a word most associated with Louis van Gaal’s time at the club, and was rejected by players and fans alike.
United have an inbuilt philosophy and identity that buys players and managers time, built on attacking football and endless running.

The modern trend towards a high press should suit that mentality. To do that, Pochettino needs to unite the sleeping giants of Manchester. How long he will have to do so, based on the patience shown with his predecessors, is, however, anyone’s guess.

articles.headline: Appeals court considers creating separate transgender cell blocks within women’s prisons
keyFacts: A federal appeals court weighed creating specialized cell blocks inside women's prisons to house transgender inmates during oral arguments on Friday.
Transgender inmates argued that transfers to men's facilities risk rape, while female prisoners reported experiencing sexual abuse from transgender inmates.
Female plaintiffs in a related case are seeking to vacate regulations allowing the Bureau of Prisons to place biological men in women's prisons.
body: A federal appeals court is weighing how to house a group of transgender inmates, all biological men currently residing in women’s prisons across the country, who are suing to prevent the Trump administration from sending them back to male-designated facilities.
The trans litigants allege under the “cruel and unusual punishment” clause of the Eighth Amendment that imprisoning them with fellow biological men would place them at a heightened risk of rape.

A three-judge panel on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit heard oral arguments on Friday in the case, Jane Doe v. Blanche , laying out creative alternatives to resolve the fear-of-rape claims.

In a rare move, the appellate panel, composed of two Trump appointees and one Obama-nominated judge, also granted speaking time to female inmates from a separate but related transgender prison separation lawsuit out of Texas .

The incarcerated women in that case, Fleming v. Warden T. Rule , succeeded in separating the biological men from the female prisoners housed there through the creation of a specialized unit inside Federal Medical Center-Carswell, a women’s prison in Fort Worth. Their case centered on witness testimony from female inmates reporting they have experienced sexual abuse at the hands of the biological men housed with them.
DOJ’S CREATIVE SOLUTION TO TRANSGENDER PRISON CASE WOULD MOVE MALE INMATES INTO SPECIALIZED UNIT

Judge Gregory Katsas, an appointee of President Donald Trump, noted during oral arguments that the Federal Bureau of Prisons was able to keep the biological men as well as the women safe at FMC-Carswell by placing the trans inmates in the specially-designed cell block.

“BOP has basically built within a women’s facility a jail within a jail for these gender dysphoric men, and they have managed to both protect these individuals from the risk [of rape] in the more violent male prisons and — just as important — protect the female inmates from the gender dysphoric man,” Katsas said.

Katsas drilled the Justice Department on why the federal government cannot create similar segregated living quarters at other women’s prisons. Government attorneys, however, remained adamant about moving the trans inmates to men’s facilities in accordance with Trump’s January 2025 directive to separate federal prisons by biological sex.

“You acknowledge they need a lot of protections there,” Katsas said. “You say that you will ramp up protections if things don’t work in the two facilities you’ve chosen, and that might push you, as you said, to something like you put them in the SHU.”

A special housing unit is a secure area used by BOP for de-escalation purposes that separates inmates from the general prison population, either placing them alone in solitary confinement or with a cellmate.

“You have arrangements that look like a prison within a prison in the male facility. So what’s the difference?” Katsas questioned. “What’s the constitutional difference? What do you care about whether the prison within the prison is at Carswell or in Rochester?”

Eric McArthur, an attorney in the DOJ’s civil division, had suggested transferring the trans complainants to an “ extraordinarily safe ” men’s prison in Rochester, Minnesota, for inmates with medical or mental health issues.

McArthur told Katsas he suspects the inmates in the Doe case will protest the idea of a miniature transgender prison, wherever the location. “You’re not going to hear from the plaintiffs that that’s a viable option,” McArthur replied. “They have filed a motion saying that even that violates [their rights].”

“I’m going to ask them about that,” Katsas said, “but I want to ask you: What’s wrong with the Fleming -Carswell arrangement from your perspective? The women are protected, and so are these plaintiffs.”

McArthur acknowledged that the FMC Carswell set-up “largely serves the government’s interest in protecting the well-being of the women,” but he argued it’s “still intruding” on BOP’s administrative authority and discretion to assign housing as it sees fit, taking into account the competing interests of all parties.

“It’s not at all clear to me that these plaintiffs, for example, are better off in a segregated unit in Carswell than in one of these extraordinarily safe men’s facilities, where they would have more freedom to move about, a wider circle of inmates with whom to socialize, and at the end of the day, if it’s necessary to protect them in the men’s facilities by putting them in a segregated unit there that’s similar to the segregated unit in the women’s facility in Carswell,” said McArthur. “I don’t see a great deal of difference between that, and I don’t think the Eighth Amendment dictates that choice and requires that they be kept in the women’s facility, segregated unit, as opposed to the men’s facility.”
A Federal Bureau of Prisons truck drives past barbed wire fences at the Federal Medical Center prison in Fort Worth, Texas, Saturday, May 16, 2020. (LM Otero/AP Photo)
Katsas later pressed Doe attorney Jennifer Levi, of the GLBTQ Advocates & Defenders, on the plaintiffs’ position on establishing Carswell-like wings dedicated to housing the trans inmates.
Levi cited “suicide risks that would be realized” upon their transfers to men’s facilities and gender dysphoria being exacerbated by the transfers themselves.
“If you think that no accommodation in a male facility is possible, your case has a lot of force, but then the only way to reconcile the competing interests is the Carswell solution,” Katsas said.
Levi said “the only thing” plaintiffs were asking of the court was to keep in place “a very narrow” injunction that blocks the transfer of the 11 trans plaintiffs.

The current preliminary injunction expires soon, and the trans appellees are asking for a new injunction, including a new requirement ordering BOP to move the eligible Doe co-plaintiffs out of the separate unit at FMC Carswell and into the general female population at another women’s prison.

Levi urged the court to at least affirm the existing injunction. “The injunction preserves the status quo that has been in place for years,” she said, referring to transgender housing accommodations implemented under the Obama administration.
“How many findings does one need to make the point that when you put men in the general female prison population, we are going to have serious issues, privacy issues, safety issues?” Katsas said.

Lawyers for the Fleming plaintiffs, who were denied their request to intervene in Doe but permitted to deliver oral arguments as amicus curiae , explained at Friday’s hearing how housing biological men in women’s general population harms women.

“It subjects women to voyeurism. It subjects women to forced exposure to male genitalia. It subjects them to sexualized threats and sexualized harassment,” attorney John Greil told the court. “The declarations that my clients submitted in the Fleming litigation are illustrative of these points, and the Constitution protects them from these harms.”
Following the hearing, Greil expressed hope that his clients’ appearance in the Doe case helped move the needle.

“In this case, the government has not submitted evidence of how female inmates are harmed by the presence of men,” Greil told the Washington Examiner . “The Fleming plaintiffs have bravely shared their stories, and brought those facts to light.”
Greil noted that the judges were interested in the workable alternative offered by the Fleming case and hearing the harms to women articulated.
MORE FEMALE INMATES ALLEGE SEXUAL ABUSE IN TRANSGENDER SEPARATION CASE

“I was glad to hear that the judges wanted to know about the impact on female inmates,” Greil said. “I’m thankful that they took the rare step of allowing my clients to be heard at oral argument — too often in these cases, the voices of affected women are not heard.”
The female plaintiffs in Fleming are now seeking to vacate the Obama-era regulations that allow BOP to place biological men in women’s prisons.

articles.headline: Here Are Some Super Useful Control Shortcuts GTA 6 Doesn’t Tell You About
keyFacts: A Kotaku writer shared several undocumented control shortcuts discovered in Grand Theft Auto 6 after spending over 150 hours playing the game.
Players can use specific button combinations to quickly toggle the car radio, cycle headlights, or exit vehicles without turning off the engine.
The author stated plans to continue testing random button combinations in future game sessions to find more hidden control options.
body: I’ve played over 150 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6. You might think I’ve seen it all, and that I know everything there is to know about the game. Nope! I’m still discovering new mechanics, features, and open-world moments after all this time. This includes some very handy control shortcuts I recently learned about that will make your life in Vice City a little easier.
How to quickly turn on the radio and cycle headlights while driving

First off, let’s start with the whole reason I wanted to write this blog. Did you know that you can quickly toggle your car radio on and off without having to enter a submenu? All you have to do is double-tap left on the D-pad, and Jason or Lucia will turn the radio on or off.

I had no idea you could do this until I saw people sharing it on Reddit. The game doesn’t explain this shortcut, as far as I can tell. I couldn’t even find it mentioned in the in-game help menu, which does include lots of other nifty tips and tricks.
Here’s another trick I just learned about: You can double-tap the circle/B button while in a car to cycle the headlights between off, high beams, and low beams.

I thought you had to hold left on the D-pad to open up the vehicle submenu to turn off the headlights, but nope! And again, this isn’t mentioned in the help menu and if a prompt appeared during the normal course of the game to explain this, I and many others must have missed it.
How to yell at drivers and exit vehicles without turning off the engine
Here’s another useful thing you can do inside cars: If you double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving, you’ll exit the vehicle without turning off the engine or radio.

GTA 6‘s help menu does call this out and mentions you can do this at speed to have your car drive into something while you roll out the side to safely. But again, I can’t remember a single time when the game forced me to do this or taught me that it was possible. I learned from a random post online. I guess I should have dug through the help menu more, but come on, who is doing that in Grand Theft Auto?

Another feature mentioned in the help menu that I just learned about is the ability to click the right stick in and yell at nearby drivers. Rockstar refers to this as the road rage button, and it’s a good thing to have in a game where NPC drivers, inspired by real Floridian drivers, suck shit and drive like maniacs.
One more useful control trick: You can double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving a boat to get up and walk around the deck while the boat keeps on cruising.

The next time I boot up GTA 6, I’m going to start double-tapping random buttons during different parts of the game to see what other hidden shortcuts and control options Rockstar has buried in this massive game. And if you want some more useful hidden features, check out this blog about how to flip cars and sit anywhere you want in GTA 6.Â
