articles.headline: Trump turns White House press conference into a 2028 succession audition
keyFacts: Donald Trump held a White House press conference alongside potential 2028 presidential contenders JD Vance and Marco Rubio.
Vice-President Vance and Secretary of State Rubio each addressed reporters to praise Trump's policies and defend his record.
Trump declined to endorse either official as his successor and jokingly asked if aide Stephen Miller should run for president instead.
body: “Which of you shall we say doth love us most?”
The ageing King Lear’s question to his daughters, expecting them to compete for his favour and carve up his kingdom, hovered in the White House press briefing room on Friday.

There at the lectern stood Donald “Lear” Trump. Behind him stood his potential heirs, JD “Goneril” Vance and Marco “Regan” Rubio, and to the side sat Trump’s favourite offspring, Stephen “Cordelia” Miller (more of him later). As for Lear’s Fool, the choices were endless.

Ostensibly this was a press conference to trumpet the president’s trip in Asia, but in practice everyone knew it was the first audition for the 2028 presidential election (and boy, is Trump going to enjoy turning the race into a contest for his approval). Vance is widely expected to seek the crown, though it was Rubio who came out on top in the latest Emerson College national poll.

In a jam-packed room, Trump stood centre stage as if hosting The Apprentice all over again. Behind him were the two contenders expressing their aspirations through matching suits, matching Maga red ties, matching US flag pins and matching leather shoes.

The first trial: could Vance and Rubio stand still for 90 minutes without rolling their eyes, yawning or silently mouthing “Kill me!” to the press? Could they force Trump’s word salad down their throats and look as if they were enjoying it? Even when the boss was rambling at length about potholes?

“When you fix a pothole”, began one detour by the octogenarian president. “I don’t want to bore you – they’ll say, oh, he rambled, he rambled terribly. I don’t ramble. I don’t ramble at all, but when you fix a pothole, you have brand new asphalt against old white asphalt that doesn’t look good, but at least you don’t ruin your car, but these roads were flawless …”

But first, the whole thing got off to a strange start. Trump appeared at the podium and remarked: “That’s a big, big a crowd. I’ve never seen this before,” but reporters crammed in the room could barely hear him above the whoosh of an air conditioning unit. An engineer tweaked the sound, but it only gave Trump’s voice an eerie echo.

Had the gremlins that grounded flights and frozen banking sites finally reached the White House? So much for America the hi-tech superpower. Eventually order was restored, though not necessarily in Trump’s brain.

He was evidently flattered by the media comparing his trilateral summit with the leaders of China and Russia to the Yalta meeting between Winston Churchill, Franklin Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin (he did not say which of the three he identified with, though critics could take a guess). Like a gushing teenager, Trump was so thrilled that Chinese president Xi Jinping had come to the airport to greet him, that he mentioned it twice (“He didn’t meet Sleepy Joe with the plane, that I can tell you.”)

The US, Russia and China hold 92% of global nuclear power, he noted, which gave him an excuse to bring up his uncle John Trump, an electrical engineer and former Massachusetts Institute of Technology professor. “A member of my family spent his life at MIT who they say is now the greatest professor in the history of MIT, so I have great understanding of- I guess maybe genetically I’m blessed,” Trump riffed.

At that remark Rubio could resist no longer. A smile spread across his lips and he shot a look at Vance, who felt obliged to smile back. We’re not laughing at you, we’re laughing with you, Mr President.

Indeed, Rubio had been the more fidgety of the pair. As Trump chuntered on, the secretary of state had shifted from foot to foot, fiddled with his tie, played with his lower lip, touched up his hair and given the odd wry smile. Vance, meanwhile, hid behind his beard and miasma of smugness.

But then, at last, came the moment for Lear’s daughters to make their public declarations of love. Vance went up the lectern and pointed out that he had stayed in Washington rather than joining the trip, comparing himself to Macaulay Culkin’s character in Home Alone – a child who is accidentally left behind at Christmas as his family rushes to catch a flight to Paris. “I missed you, sir,” he said to Trump, before praising the president for “securing historic trade deals” and reorganising the global economy to benefit the American worker and economy.

Not bad, but a little wonky. Marco, you’re up next. The secretary of state took aim at the critics who accused Trump of cosying up to dictators at the expense of Democrats, raising his eyebrows and shaking his fist: “These three countries possess the overwhelming majority of nuclear weapons on this planet. The idea that these three leaders should not engage on a regular basis is not just absurd, it’s dangerous.”

Trump began taking reporters’ questions. One young whippersnapper posed a question that will be asked many times over the next two years. “Because you have the vice-president, the secretary of state right behind you, I’m curious which of them do you think would make a better president after you?”
Trump swatted it aside without answering. Vance remained stony faced. Rubio smiled knowingly.

The same reporter put Vance in an uncomfortable spot by asking about his post-midterm tweet. “Would you argue that the war in Iran was worth it to lose the Senate?” The vice-president agreed with the goal of Iran not getting a nuclear weapon but added carefully: “I think the president is the one who makes the decision and the president has said he would do it again. And my view is that my goal is and my job is to support the president of the United States.”
In other words, I hate this war and would never have started it but I have to back the boss. Expect a lot more of this needle-threading in the upcoming campaign.

Later, when Trump asked “Do you want to keep this going or not” amid a cacophony of shouted questions, he turned around to look at Rubio, who laughed, then at Vance, who did likewise with folded arms. The two rivals patted each other playfully. But neither was prepared for the man who would steal their thunder.

“We have the most powerful man in the world in the room right now,” said Trump, referring to Miller, the recently appointed White House chief of ideological zealotry, who stepped up to the lectern with bald pate gleaming under the bright lights.

“I just wanted to say that what President Trump has achieved over the last two years is more than any president has achieved by far in American history!” Miller roared, before offering the kind of vainglorious soliloquy that would make even a Kremlin or Chinese Communist party spokesperson blush. “What you’re going to see over the next two years, as astonishing as that has been under his leadership, the next two years are going to be the greatest two years in American history!”

Trump, who loves nothing more than flattery with exclamation marks, returned to the lectern and announced: “We have breaking news. We have breaking news.” Waving his hands, then with thumbs pointed at Vance and Rubio, he said of Miller: “He was better than these two guys. Do you want to run for president?”

That was a joke, right? Trump was stirring the succession pot again, making his potential heirs uncomfortable. It was fitting that he ended the press conference reminiscing about the night he hosted Ultimate Fighting Championship bouts on the White House South Lawn. He is going to relish every moment of presiding over a Republican cage match for the next two years.

articles.headline: Can AI really help spot Black Friday deals? We put it to the test
keyFacts: BBC tests of four major AI chatbots for Black Friday deals found mixed results, including broken retailer links and inaccurate prices.
Consumer group Which? warned that inaccurate chatbot pricing wastes time for Black Friday shoppers trying to find budget deals.
Business advisor Naureen Mohammed said she suspects advertising models will start influencing future chatbot shopping recommendations.
body: - Published
Whether it's scrolling through endless choice, spotting fake reviews, or working out if a "deal" is a deal at all, Black Friday sums up a lot of online woes.
Retailers promise bargains - but the sheer number of offers can leave us feeling no closer to finding the best deal.
It's an area where generative AI products, such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, have promised to help.
But are they any good at finding Black Friday deals? We had a go ourselves a week ahead of the big day.
Figures suggest relatively few UK shoppers currently go to AI tools for help.
A recent YouGov survey of 19 countries found the UK ranked second-last in the proportion of people who said they had used AI to help them shop.
Crucially, 36% of respondents who said they would be shopping around Black Friday didn't plan to use an AI tool at all.
But the survey suggested a growing number of people were considering it - and tech firms have released features to capitalise on this.
Amazon launched Alexa for Shopping for UK users in November and OpenAI launched a Shopping Research tool on ChatGPT days before last year's Black Friday.
In the US, Google recently launched Universal Cart, with AI-powered features such as price tracking and identification of relevant promo codes.
But there has been criticism that fact-checking AI ends up taking more time, while some brands are working to try to make sure their products show up in chatbot answers.
We asked four models to find a 55-inch TV deal, using the free versions of many of the most popular tools.
While this was not a rigorous scientific test, the experience we had produced mixed results.
ChatGPT - full price and not available to buy
OpenAI's ChatGPT came up with four options.
Its top pick was a Hisense TV on Chinese retailer Joybuy's website, on sale for Â£499 down from Â£649.
The next recommendation was a 55-inch TCL-branded TV, but a sidebar showed prices for the 50-inch version, from Â£379 to Â£814.
Option three was the same Hisense TV as before, but for full price at Â£649 from John Lewis and Richer Sounds.
This was the "best safer purchase" according to ChatGPT, as the sites offered longer guarantee periods.
But clicking on the links did not go well. Both retailers said the TV was no longer listed online.
The fourth option was equally fruitless - another TCL TV, at full price, Â£150 over our budget and not available online.
At the bottom, ChatGPT served one last offer - "one OLED option to compare" - for a Â£1,100 LG TV that was marked as "Ad".
Claude - honest, but not too helpful
Claude produced the shortest answer of all the models we tested, and unlike the others, it did not give much detail on the specifications of each model.
Instead, it seemed to base its results on a small number of reviews published online.
It recommended the same two TCL TVs as ChatGPT.
But when we clicked on the links, they sent us to two dead pages on the Richer Sounds website.
Some other links led to year-old round-ups of Black Friday 2025 deals.
Claude was not very enthusiastic about its other two recommendations due to a lack of independent reviews - calling one "a decent option" but saying it "wouldn't pick" the other.
It also listed two Samsung TVs, but it told us not to buy them, with one "over budget and not clearly better than the TCLs".
We were left wondering why it even mentioned them in the first place.
Gemini - a familiar pattern
Different AI model, same TV manufacturers - albeit different Hisense and TCL models to the previous chatbots' recommendations.
Gemini generated a table comparing four different models, but offered no links to the stores it named, so we searched for them ourselves.
The prices for one TCL TV were correct at Â£649, but it was sold out at one of the named retailers.
It said the other TCL model was available from Argos and Currys for Â£539 - correct for Argos, but when we checked Currys, it was Â£60 more expensive.
Again, it included two Samsung models to avoid due to lower screen specs.
Alexa - accurate but limited
Alexa came back with four TVs, from its own Amazon Ember at Â£532 to a Â£699 Samsung.
But its top recommendation was to go for another Samsung model at Â£616 (down from Â£749), based on its picture quality and Amazon customer rating.
Its fourth option was for a Sony TV, but it was only 50 inches, leaving us unsure why it had included it.

All the prices stated were correct, but Amazon only searches its own store. Alexa did acknowledge this, encouraging us to check its rivals for better deals, "as prices can vary" and we could get longer guarantees elsewhere.
Inconsistent pricing
There are methods that can boost the likelihood of getting a better response, from crafting more informative prompts to upping a chatbot's "thinking" level.
Tech journalist Alex Hughes had better luck than we did when he used ChatGPT's agentic AI mode to find a TV in last year's Black Friday sales.
Agentic AI is still in its early days, but it allows AI to act with more autonomy and carry out multi-step tasks.
The search took about 20 minutes "with very little work on my end needed," Hughes wrote for Tom's Guide, external in November 2025.
A year on, he told the BBC he didn't go through with buying a TV at that time.
He did later purchase one of the seven models ChatGPT had surfaced - but he had found it for a lower price in a bricks-and-mortar shop.
Will he be using AI to find Black Friday deals again this year? "Probably not," he said.
He reckoned it saved him time, but "when you're trying to deal with something like live price data... it will be inconsistent and quite often incorrect".
Slim pickings
While we were served up the same brands again and again, in reality there are tonnes of products listed for sale around Black Friday.
Naureen Mohammed, who advises businesses on how to get their products to appear in AI results, told the BBC customers did not see the full picture when they talked to chatbots.
If businesses fail to update their prices when people start hunting for bargains, "last year's prices are served up as today's deals".
"I suspect the whole model for advertising is going to start influencing AI recommendations," she said.
Her own analysis of chatbots' Black Friday tech deals in the UK suggested the big retailers came out on top - with Amazon mentioned in half of responses, and Currys following closely behind.
Her tips include asking an assistant "is that this year's price?" and clicking on the links provided - "because you shouldn't take any advice from the AI system at face value".
But consumer group Which? recently said inaccurate pricing in AI results added more work, external to Black Friday deal-hunting.

"If you ask ChatGPT for a list of 10 laptops under Â£400 and seven of the results are priced higher, you've likely wasted a good chunk of time going through them to discover the bot gave you only three options," said senior researcher Hannah Walsh.
"The opposite is also true - you could miss out on great models in your budget if ChatGPT tells you they are more expensive than they actually are."

articles.headline: US judge approves Bayer's $7.25 billion cancer settlement
keyFacts: A US judge approved Bayer's $7.25 billion settlement resolving lawsuits claiming its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer.
The agreement covers tens of thousands of people who say they developed non-Hodgkin lymphoma after using Roundup.
Bayer will pay the funds over 21 years, though the approval ruling could still be appealed.
body: A US judge on Friday approved German chemical giant Bayer's $7.25 billion (€6.60 billion) settlement of lawsuits claiming its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer.
Judge Timothy Boyer in the US state of Missouri ruled that the agreement was "fair, reasonable, and adequate."
The decision could help Bayer end years of costly legal battles over Roundup, which the company acquired when it bought US weedkiller producer Monsanto in 2018.
"The court's final approval is a decisive milestone in the company's strategy to mitigate the risks of both pending and future Roundup litigation," Bayer CEO Bill Anderson said.
The ruling could still be appealed.
How much money will Roundup cancer patients receive?
The agreement covers tens of thousands of people who say they developed non-Hodgkin lymphoma, a type of blood cancer, after using Roundup.
It also covers people who may be diagnosed with the disease in the future after previous exposure to the weedkiller.
Bayer will pay up to $7.25 billion into a special fund over the next 21 years.

Individual payments are expected to average between $10,000 and $165,000. The amount will depend on factors including the patient's age, the severity of the illness and how long they were exposed to Roundup.
Some lawyers representing cancer patients have criticized the payments as too low.
But the judge rejected their objections, saying that further delays could leave seriously ill patients waiting years for compensation.
Christopher Seeger, a lawyer representing cancer patients, welcomed the decision.
"Today's final approval order delivers guaranteed compensation to Roundup cancer victims who have waited more than a decade for justice," he said.
Why has it become harder to sue Bayer over Roundup?
The settlement follows a major victory for Bayer at the US Supreme Court in June.
The court ruled that Bayer could not be sued under state laws for failing to put cancer warnings on Roundup packaging.
The judges argued that US federal rules did not require such warnings and that individual states could not impose additional labeling requirements.
The decision made it much harder for cancer patients to win lawsuits against Bayer.
In October, a Missouri jury also ruled in Bayer's favor in a separate Roundup cancer case.
However, some legal battles continue. Around 200 cases are still being fought in federal courts outside the new settlement, according to Bayer.
How much have the Roundup lawsuits cost Bayer?
Monsanto introduced Roundup in 1974. Its main ingredient, glyphosate, became one of the world's most widely used weedkillers.
Farmers use Roundup to kill weeds without damaging crops that have been genetically modified to survive the chemical. It has also been widely used in private gardens and on lawns.
Bayer inherited the legal problems surrounding Roundup when it bought Monsanto for $63 billion in 2018.
Since then, around 200,000 claims have been made against Bayer by people who believe the weedkiller caused their cancer.
The company already agreed to a $10.9 billion settlement in 2020. However, it failed to secure approval for a separate agreement covering future cases.
Some lawsuits have resulted in huge payouts, including a $2.1 billion award to plaintiffs in Georgia.
Bayer has already set aside $16 billion for Roundup-related legal costs. Its shares have fallen by 46% since the Monsanto takeover.
The company has also removed glyphosate from newer versions of Roundup sold to private consumers in the United States.
Does Roundup really cause cancer?
Scientists and regulators disagree about whether glyphosate causes cancer.
In 2015, the World Health Organization's cancer research agency classified the chemical as "probably carcinogenic" to humans.
However, the US Environmental Protection Agency says glyphosate is unlikely to cause cancer when used as directed.
Bayer has repeatedly denied that Roundup causes cancer, pointing to scientific studies and regulatory approvals.
The debate intensified last year when a major scientific study that had supported Roundup's safety for decades was withdrawn.
The journal that published it cited serious problems, including missing cancer research and previously undisclosed involvement by Monsanto employees.
The withdrawal raised further questions about the influence of chemical companies on scientific research.

articles.headline: Even the Iconic Google Home Page Can’t Survive the Push for More AI
keyFacts: Google is rolling out desktop homepage AI buttons worldwide for image creation, file analysis, and brainstorming.
Google Search Product VP Robby Stein announced a collapsible sidebar showing recent AI search threads to help users track progress.
Three major school districts reported they may switch search engines because Google will not provide a chatbot-free search tool for students.
body: This is not your parents’ Google home page. In its push to get more users to adopt its AI tools, the search engine giant is rolling out a raft of new features worldwide.

The new elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm. The Google Search button is gone, but the I’m Feeling Lucky button remains.
The buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile. I was able to see the new buttons when signed in to my Google account.
More from CNET
When signed out, I was only able to see the typical home page, with the only AI button being AI Mode, which has been there since May 2025.
What do the new buttons do?

Clicking on the “Create images” button opens up a new page where you can create an AI-generated image using Google’s Nano Banana. It’s the same image-generation tool you can use on other Google platforms such as the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and AI Mode in Search.

Clicking “Ask about files” allows for several options. You can have the AI analyze a document and rewrite it, simply have it answer questions or ask it to perform tasks such as “polish my resume” or “draft an email with action items.”
The “Brainstorm” button prompts you to “describe your goal,” such as making a to-do list, learning how to code or finding a table at a restaurant.
And there’s more

Another new feature, as announced by Google Search Product VP Robby Stein on X, is a collapsible sidebar on the left side of the home page, which shows your recent AI search threads and offers the ability to create a new one:
Stein said the new sidebar will help users go back to where they left off.
“People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done — and in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web,” Stein posted.
I didn’t see the collapsible sidebar during my testing of the home page.
Data privacy concerns

Google will use your AI searches — whether they are questions, tasks, uploaded files or image generation — to train its AI models, but you can tell Google you’re opting out. CNET has an overview of how to tell chatbots not to use your data. Still, for Google specifically, you can go to Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity to turn off AI training.
Google’s AI push

Google has integrated its Gemini AI models throughout its various platforms — Search, Gmail, Docs, Pixel phones and third-party apps such as Adobe, Shopify, OpenTable and Instacart. This past week, Google announced several other new AI features — integrations with stores such as Albertsons, Safeway and Target to complete orders and connect to apps such as Peloton and Adobe.
Over the summer, Google’s Gemini app topped 1 billion users in what CEO Sundar Pichai called the company’s “fastest growing product ever.”

But Google’s rush to force-feed AI into its products has met with plenty of pushback. The New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago school districts said they might choose different search engines because Google said it will not remove AI from search tools used by students, The New York Times reported.

Google said search and the Gemini app will be turned off for schools unless school administrators want them. But Google said there will not be a chatbot-free version of search available for schools. So schools declining AI will not be able to search using Google at all.

Google’s AI Overviews, which appear at the top of many search page results, have also been blamed for a steep drop in web traffic to content publishers. AI Overviews summarize user search queries and replace the long list of blue hyperlinks that once appeared across search pages. So instead of clicking on those links to get more information, giving publishers valuable clicks, a user can simply get their query response by reading the AI Overview.

articles.headline: The Official Lord of the Rings Pizza Cutter Drops to a New Low Price at Amazon
keyFacts: Amazon reduced the price of the official Lord of the Rings pizza cutter by 20 percent to $159.99.
Manufacturer Dalstrong builds the pizza cutter using German X50CrMoV15 steel and features an ebony wood handle with engraved designs.
The pizza wheel package includes a collector pin, a leather sheath, and premium gift packaging.
body: Amazon's Black Friday sale is a great time to find discounts on things you actually need. It's also a great time to buy expensive gifts for yourself that you absolutely don't need. Somewhere in between those two extremes is where I like to do most of my online window shopping, which is what led me to this discount on the official Lord of the Rings Pizza Wheel.

Amazon is currently offering a 20% discount, which drops the price down to $159.99 for the first time ever. It's a very expensive pizza cutter for sure, but it's also one of the coolest LOTR gifts for your kitchen you'll find anywhere.

As someone who makes a lot of pizzas at home, I can attest to how important it is to have a good pizza cutter at your disposal. If you don't have a sharp enough blade, toppings get crushed and pepperonis do that thing where they disappear into the cracks of every cut. You're only going to get good pizza slices if you have a knife capable of cutting good slices.

Dalstrong, the brand who makes this product, uses high-quality German X50CrMoV15 steel for their knives and pizza cutters. This gives them solid toughness and corrosion resistance that will help keep the blade sharper for longer. This type of steel isn't going to hold an edge nearly as long as the high-end Japanese variety, but it's fairly easy to sharpen and hone at home if the edge does get dull. Just don't go putting it in the dishwasher!

As for the LOTR stuff that actually makes this pizza cutter cool, there's a lot to love in the design. The handle is made of ebony wood and copper accents with the Leaf of Lórien carved into it. The blade itself is left bare to ensure drag-free cutting, but both sides include different designs etched into the steel. On one side you get silhouettes of the members of The Fellowship of the Ring and on the other side you get an inscription written in Elvish. I can't actually read Elvish, but I hope it just says pizza multiple times.

The pizza wheel also comes with a collector's pin and a leather sheath to help protect the blade. The whole thing ships in the kind of premium gift packaging that you'd expect from a nearly $200 pizza cutter.
The 4K Movie Trilogy Is Also on Sale Today

Amazon also has a great deal on the 4K collection going on right now that's worth checking out. This includes both the theatrical and extended editions of the film in full 4K UHD. If you're only streaming these movies with an HBO Max subscription, you're missing out on the full visual experience.

articles.headline: Why you shouldn't depend on GTA 6 to auto-save
keyFacts: Grand Theft Auto 6 auto-saves after major events, purchases, or deaths rather than at regular time intervals.
The save system has caused several people to lose hours of progress because the game never auto-saves during missions.
To avoid losing progress, players can save manually using fifteen available manual save slots in the game menu.
body: Why you shouldn't depend on GTA 6 to auto-save
It's not on a timer.

In addition to getting your boss to let you take time off to play Grand Theft Auto 6, one of the more frightening prospects of playing games like GTA 6 is trusting the auto-save feature. It's been part of so many games for literal decades, but it's really found its home in big, expansive open-world games like the GTA series. The old mantra of auto-save, then manual save twice just to be sure, still rings true today.

As ever, depending on auto save to make sure your journey through Vice City is like depending on Rockstar to release something quickly. It's not a tremendously wise idea, and with GTA 6, Rockstar has implemented an auto save that certainly functions, but maybe not in the same way you may have grown accustomed to in other games.

If you're already tens of hours deep in your journey through the criminal underworld, it may be wise to stick around for a moment. Here's what we know about how the saving system works, and what you can do to make sure your progress isn't lost.
An explanation of the auto save system in GTA 6

Grand Theft Auto 6's auto-save feature may not work as you think. Instead of automatically saving at regular intervals, the game appears to save after every main mission, as well as after some major side missions, expensive purchases, or when you get killed or arrested. That means if you're roaming the map, getting into trouble or driving around, the game relies on you to save manually. Unfortunately, the auto-save icon (a white spinning circle) doesn't always show up when the game saves.

GTA 6 has one auto-save slot, which it overwrites each time, and 15 manual slots. To manually save, press the Options button on PS5 or the Menu button on Xbox, then go to the Game tab and choose Save Game.

The unusual auto-save system has caused several people to lose hours of progress, although in the bigger picture of a game that's sold in the millions, it's thankfully not too widespread. One save tip from our editors playing through the game: GTA 6 doesn't auto-save in the middle of a mission, period.

If you're cruising the streets of Vice City and worry about a power outage, or if you're someone who turns the console off without thinking, remember to save manually. The same goes when you strike it big and get your hands on the ride of your dreams or clear one of the countless side missions: Save regularly to keep your GTA 6 journey going and your sanity intact.

articles.headline: Amazon's split personality: AWS embraces bot commerce while main site enforces bans
keyFacts: Amazon banned AI shopping agents from its main website while allowing bot-based purchases on AWS Marketplace.
AWS Marketplace allows AI agents to search and purchase cloud software products using the x402 payment protocol.
Product marketing manager Mya Papolu announced that AWS Marketplace is now selling data as a service to AI agents.
body: Amazon is of two minds when it comes to automated purchasing. The ecommerce giant has been busy banning AI shopping agents from accessing its website. Meanwhile, AWS Marketplace has opened its door to bot-based buying.

"Buying software and data through AWS Marketplace just got easier, for you and for the AI agents working alongside you," said Mya Papolu, product marketing manager for AWS Marketplace and Partner Services at Amazon Web Services, in a blog post this week. "For re:Invent 2026, we’re launching capabilities designed to reduce friction across the buying journey."

For a company that has blocked bots from Google, Meta, and OpenAI, and sued Perplexity to keep its AI-encumbered Comet browser away, the openness of AWS Marketplace to agentic commerce invites questions.
We asked Amazon to explain but we've not heard back.
AWS Marketplace is allowing AI agents to scour its site and buy some cloud software products using the x402 agentic payment protocol , which is supported by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments.

Introduced by Coinbase and Cloudflare , x402 got handed over to the Linux Foundation earlier this year, and now has support from a variety of tech platforms, including AWS, Google, Stripe, and various blockchain networks. About a week ago, Brave Software announced support for x402 payments through its search API.

AWS requires sellers to register with AWS Marketplace and to integrate the AWS Marketplace x402 SDK to enable agentic product purchases. Transactions settle in USD through AWS billing so existing spending controls can be applied.
And now, customers in the US can buy some AWS Marketplace software without an AWS account; instead they're asked to provide an email or social media login, and a credit card.

While AWS Marketplace today lists mainly familiar software categories (Business Applications, Data & Analytics, DevOps, Infrastructure Software, and so on), AWS has a broader product inventory in mind. Beyond software and APIs, the biz sees a future in selling content and data.
Papolu announced that AWS is now selling " data as a service ."

"Data providers can list their offerings in AWS Marketplace, making commercial data accessible to both human teams and the agents working alongside them via the AWS Marketplace website, APIs, and MCP server," she said.

This includes services like Moody's Credit MCP server for financial research; Reuters Geopolitical News for AI-structured reporting; US Building Permits, Contractors & Residents Data from Shovels; and US-EN Multi-Speaker Conversational Acoustic Corpus from Uber AI Solutions.
In canned remarks provided to AWS, Nandhan Puppala, general manager at Uber AI Solutions, said that data quality and readiness can help advance AI products.

Agent mode for AWS Marketplace has been available for about a year as a way to query the market via prompt. That's being expanded to allow deeper queries about seller security and project requirements.
Science fiction writer William Gibson's oft-cited line , "The future is already here – it's just not very evenly distributed" appears to apply to Amazon. ®

articles.headline: Texas Gov-elect Gina Hinojosa vows to rescind Abbott's H-1B visa restrictions despite admitting program abuse
keyFacts: Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa stated she plans to rescind Governor Greg Abbott's H-1B visa hiring freeze on her first day in office.
Abbott said his directive protects domestic jobs from being displaced by lower-paid foreign workers at state agencies and public universities.
Hinojosa acknowledged company abuses exist within the program, but she intends to overturn the freeze scheduled through May 2027.
body: Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa (D) said she plans to rescind Gov. Greg Abbott’s hiring freeze on H-1B visa workers at state agencies and public universities on her first day in office, even as she acknowledged that the federal visa program has been abused.
In a recent interview with the Texas Tribune, Hinojosa, a Democrat, dismissed Abbott’s January directive restricting new H-1B visa petitions as a distraction.
"Yeah, that does not make sense to me. I will tell you, I’m not doing culture wars. That’s not what I was elected to do," Hinojosa said.

Abbott issued the order in January to bar state agencies and public universities from filing new H-1B petitions without written approval from the Texas Workforce Commission, citing reports that employers had displaced U. S. workers with lower-paid foreign labor.
OBAMA-APPOINTED JUDGE TORPEDOES TRUMP’S BID TO PROTECT US JOBS BY REFORMING CONTROVERSIAL IMMIGRATION POLICY
"In the most egregious schemes, employers have even fired American workers and replaced them with H-1B employees , often at lower wages," Abbott wrote in his January directive.
While Hinojosa vowed to scrap the restrictions, she conceded that companies have exploited the visa system.

"There are abuses when it comes to H-1Bs, absolutely," Hinojosa told the Texas Tribune. "Companies should not be getting a bunch of tax breaks for jobs to only then use that money to hire H-1B employees. That’s wrong. That’s happening right now. I don’t support that."

Hinojosa, a Democratic state representative from Austin, defeated Abbott in the Nov. 3 election to deny the three-term Republican incumbent a fourth term, becoming the first Democrat elected governor of Texas since Ann Richards in 1990. With Republicans still holding a majority in the Texas Senate, rescinding Abbott’s executive orders offers Hinojosa an immediate way to reshape state policy without legislative approval.
HISTORIC GOP DEFEAT FUELS 11TH-HOUR POWER STRUGGLE AS NEW ALLIES RALLY TO REIN IN INCOMING DEM GOVERNOR

Hinojosa also defended local school districts’ use of H-1B visas to recruit foreign educators, arguing that Texas schools struggle to find domestic teachers. Abbott’s directive, however, applies only to state agencies and public institutions of higher education, not local K-12 school districts.
A representative for Hinojosa did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Abbott’s freeze was scheduled to remain in place through May 31, 2027, to give lawmakers time to pass broader reforms, while requiring affected agencies and universities to report their current H-1B visa holders and efforts to recruit qualified Texas residents.

articles.headline: Cost of Man Utd hiring and firing managers nears £100m
keyFacts: Manchester United borrowed 10m pounds shortly after hiring Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach.
United will pay 7.5m pounds in compensation to US Soccer to secure Pochettino.
The total cost of hiring and firing managers since 2013 has reached 95m pounds and is expected to exceed 100m pounds.
body: - Published
Manchester United borrowed another Â£10m three days after confirming Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach.

In an extended Stock Market filing to go with their first-quarter financial results that were released on Thursday, United said they would be liable to pay Â£7.5m in compensation to US Soccer to hire the Argentine.
United announced Pochettino had agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal on 13 November. They borrowed Â£10m on 16 November.
The loan is one of three confirmed after the 30 September first-quarter reporting date, which takes the overall amount owed on their rolling credit limit to Â£240m.

The amount paid to release Pochettino from his USA deal takes the sums paid hiring and firing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 to Â£95m. However, that figure is likely to top Â£100m once the cost of hiring Pochettino's staff and sacking Michael Carrick is added.

Carrick was sacked last week with the club in the relegation zone and enduring their worst start to a season in 40 years. The former midfielder only signed a two-year contract in the summer after a successful six-month spell in caretaker charge last season.
Pochettino is the ninth full-time manager to be appointed since Ferguson, including Ralf Rangnick in November 2021. United have changed their manager in the middle of the last three campaigns.
The club also confirmed they had spent Â£5.7m to either acquire or extend registrations of "certain players and members of coaching staff".

The filing also revealed they owe Â£417m in outstanding transfer fees, Â£181m of which is due after one year. United said on Thursday their substantial $750m debt was Â£577.4m when converted to sterling on 30 September.

articles.headline: Trump Insists Putin Is His 'Friend,' But Admits He ‘Can’t Speak To America’
keyFacts: Donald Trump stated he has a very good relationship with Vladimir Putin after reporters asked about their interactions in China.
When asked if Putin is a friend to America, Trump responded that he cannot speak to America.
Trump defended his ties with Russia, stating it is beneficial to have relationships with leaders of the most powerful countries.
body: Donald Trump keeps figuring out new ways to shock people on social media, but a comment he made Friday about Russian president Vladimir Putin was in another league altogether.
The president held a press conference on Friday, a day after he met Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, and was asked about his relationship with the Russian leader.
CNN’s Kaitlan Collins — a popular Trump target — noted that, while in China, Trump said Putin was his “friend,” before noting that Russia is Iran’s biggest ally.
“Do you believe Putin is a friend to America?” she asked bluntly.
In response, Trump seemed to suggest that it’s none of America’s concern what people think of his relationship with Putin.

“I can’t speak to America. I’ve been dealing with Putin during the fake ‘Russia, Russia, Russia’ hoax. And to be honest, he was very nice about it,” Trump said, before adding that he considers the Russian president “somebody that I have a very good relationship [with].”
Trump then appeared to sympathize with Putin for getting into a war with Ukraine, which he said, ”should have lasted one day and it’s lasted for five years.”

ABC News reporter Rachel Scott continued the questioning, and Trump freely admitted he’s “so nice to Russia,” stressing, “It’s a good thing that I have a relationship,” insisting that, “You’re very lucky to have somebody that has a relationship with the heads of the most powerful countries.”

HuffPost reached out to the White House for comment, but no one immediately responded.
Not surprisingly, many people on social media were aghast at Trump’s comments, with some suggesting that he cares more about a Russian president than his own citizens.

articles.headline: Why everyone, even the GOP, is sick of JD Vance
keyFacts: Vox reported that Vice President JD Vance faces tension with President Donald Trump over differing stances on the Iran war and immigration.
An Emerson College poll showed Vance's 2028 primary support dropped to 20 percent, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio led with 36 percent.
According to media reports, Republicans including Marco Rubio, Ron DeSantis, and Ted Cruz are considering 2028 presidential bids.
body: President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance at a Veterans Day in Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026. | Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images
This story appeared in Today, Explained, a daily newsletter that helps you understand the most compelling news and stories of the day. Subscribe here .
Remember two weeks ago, when Vice President JD Vance was having a bad week ? It’s gotten much, much worse.

Vance has spent most of the last two years as the MAGA movement’s heir apparent — so much so that Secretary of State Marco Rubio, potentially his top rival for the 2028 GOP presidential nomination, told a reporter last year that “If JD Vance runs for president, he’s going to be our nominee, and I’ll be one of the first people to support him.”

Suffice to say, that no longer looks like the case: Vance, more than any other potential Republican candidate in 2028, emerged from the midterms in bad political shape, and President Donald Trump has been putting him through hell ever since.

Specifically, Vance has found himself in a trap of his own making on two issues: The Iran war and immigration. In a long social media post the day after the midterms, he blamed the war for his party’s electoral catastrophe; more recently, he described “bipartisan immigration reform” that would allow undocumented immigrants to stay in the country as “morally and electorally disastrous.”

The problem with those two stances is that he’s still Trump’s vice president, and Trump refuses to admit that the Iran war was the wrong decision (though he’s been willing enough to concede that it was an electoral anchor). Trump is also in the midst of showing occasional, vague interest in the aforementioned bipartisan immigration reform. And he’s reportedly not happy with Vance’s subtweets.

Both of those tensions were on full display Friday in a press conference by Trump, Vance, and Rubio, where Vance dodged a question on whether the war was worth the political fallout — an area where Trump has strongly suggested he’d like more backup from his second-in-command. “The president said he would do it again,” Vance told reporters. “My view is that my goal in my job is to support the president of the United States.”

That answer, you might correctly surmise, is almost certainly not going to do it with Trump over the long run. (This being the same president so bent on conforming the world around him to his views that he dispenses matching too-big shoes to his team, and they wear them.)
Vance’s double bind
Vance’s plight is particularly dire because he doesn’t really have anywhere to run. His options look something like this:

Hug Trump, hope for an endorsement, and see if the president’s reflected goodwill can push him to the nomination (and potentially to a general election wipeout, if Trump’s trajectory with voters stays the same);
Break from Trump more dramatically, forfeiting an endorsement and MAGA enthusiasm, and try to stake out his own brand in the primary and the general;
Or keep on keeping on, cryptically sniping at opponents from social media until Trump gets mad anyway.

Meanwhile, the weaker Vance looks , the more his potential rivals are likely to eye the throne for themselves. In a poll released Thursday by Emerson College , Vance’s potential 2028 support has collapsed from 54 percent this time last year to just 20 percent, while Rubio’s has jumped from 6 percent to 36 percent (more than any other polled candidate, with Vance in second). And Rubio, according to CNN , is leaving some people with the impression that he’s more open to a run.

Other Republicans, including outgoing Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis and Texas Sen. Ted Cruz, are also believed to be considering runs, and both would have the advantage of being able to run from outside a Trump administration that seems unlikely to grow more popular over the next two years.
Vance, in other words, already looks like he could be approaching his best-by date — and he still has a very long year-plus until the first votes are cast in the 2028 primary.

articles.headline: Trump FCC declares California isn't allowed to enforce phone service rules
keyFacts: The Federal Communications Commission ordered California to stop enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort rules against AT&T.
AT&T aims to discontinue basic phone service for 184,000 residential and 15,000 business customers in California by June 2027.
California could sue the commission over the order, setting up another battle over the state's telecom enforcement rights.
body: The Federal Communications Commission ordered California to stop enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort (COLR) rules against AT&T, setting up another battle between the Trump administration and California over the state’s right to enforce its own telecom laws and regulations.

AT&T’s status as a Carrier of Last Resort in California requires it to offer telephone service to any potential customer in its territory. AT&T wants to stop offering basic phone service to new customers and discontinue service for 184,000 residential customers and 15,000 business customers on June 1, 2027.

The order released today granted AT&T’s request to preempt state rules, following up on the FCC’s previous approval of AT&T’s petition to discontinue service. AT&T had tried to achieve the same result in court, but a federal judge rejected its request to override California’s rules in July.

The FCC order probably isn’t the last word, as California could sue the commission. California has stood alone against AT&T, which has received relief from COLR obligations in 20 of the 21 states in its wireline service territory.
Carr: California rules “designed for a bygone era”

“California’s Carrier of Last Resort framework may have made sense when it was established 30 years ago,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement released with today’s order. “But those rules were designed for a bygone era and no longer make sense in today’s competitive, advanced marketplace.”

If AT&T ends service on its old copper lines, many homes and businesses would not be offered modern fiber networks. AT&T claims a wireless home phone service that connects to the cellular network will be good enough, and the FCC agreed.

“The FCC has granted AT&T’s applications to replace legacy voice service with a modern, IP-based alternative in certain areas of the state. California’s state requirements are blocking AT&T from proceeding with a federally authorized transition,” Carr said.

California says its rules allow wireless replacements if they meet the state’s standards for basic phone service, but that AT&T must demonstrate that its wireless phone service would meet the COLR obligations. California’s requirements include flat-rate options for unlimited voice calls, discounted Lifeline rates for eligible low-income customers, and telephone relay service for people who are deaf and hard of hearing.

articles.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI appears to mock NFL sexual misconduct scandals in radio parody
keyFacts: Grand Theft Auto VI features a satirical radio segment that appears to mock NFL sexual misconduct scandals and related athlete defenses.
The segment features a radio host defending a fictional player who became sexually aroused during a massage, blaming the therapist instead.
The game's satire closely resembles past allegations against NFL players Deshaun Watson and Justin Tucker, both of whom faced massage-related misconduct claims.
body: The long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI appears to have taken aim at the NFL’s sexual misconduct scandals – and the culture of excuses surrounding them – with a satirical segment on the video game’s fictional conservative talk radio station bearing striking similarities to allegations against Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson and Kansas City Chiefs kicker Justin Tucker.

The segment features comedian and voice actor Stavros Halkias defending Anthony Ross, a fictional player for the Vice City Manatees, after an “alleged” incident involving a team masseuse. Although neither Watson nor Tucker are mentioned by name, the circumstances closely resemble allegations made against both players.

Halkias, voicing outspoken sports talk radio host Dominick “The Brick” Brizzolato in a withering caricature of right-wing media bombast, argues the player was not responsible for becoming sexually aroused during a massage and instead blames the therapist, in an apparent parody of the defenses offered on behalf of athletes accused of sexual misconduct.

“Be the voice of reason here,” Halkias begins. “You know, there is extreme idiocy and stupidity on both sides, folks. I mean, think. Put yourself in Ross’s shoes. OK, you’re a pro football player, a warrior in a proud tribe called the Vice City Manatees. You’re getting treated by the team masseuse after a rough game, after leaving it all out on the field. You’re on the table and your penis gets hard, allegedly.

“Is it his fault? No, it is not. He’s got testosterone coursing through his veins. He’s got the juice. The juices are flowing. He’s got elevated stress levels. The man has taken a pounding for this team and this city. His body is gonna react natural [sic]. We are talking about a peak athlete. It is not his fault for how his body naturally responds. Is it her fault for making him get an erection? Yes, I believe clearly it is.”
The in-game shock jock goes on to argue that the massage therapist should be held responsible for the incident.
“A masseuse knows what she’s doing, and she can use her bewitching touch to make him aroused,” Halkias’s character says. “We all know this. I myself have experienced this seven to eight times.”

Lamenting that teams used to “[do] the honorable thing” and fire therapists who spoke out in the interest of “protecting the players”, he adds: “It didn’t used to be about these feminists trying to latch onto a successful man and get out of their little apartment out of whatever fucking public housing, you know, one bedroom over top of whatever fucking carryout they live in.
“We used to protect the players in this country. We need to understand that when an athlete is primed up and charged and ready to go, oh, we like to see it when their muscles are big and they react.”

The rant is one of many satirical broadcasts featured in Rockstar Games’ sprawling recreation of Florida, which a Guardian editorial described as a skewering portrait of a country “awash with vice and hypocrisy”, where wealth, spectacle and criminality increasingly blur together.

In an ironic twist, Watson himself had referenced GTA VI just a day before its release. Asked on Wednesday whether the Browns, who are 6-4 and in playoff contention, had begun discussing the postseason, Watson suggested the highly anticipated video game was occupying more of his teammates’ attention. “We’re not getting ahead of ourselves. Most of the guys are thinking about GTA,” the 31-year-old said. Whether Watson or his teammates have encountered the apparent reference to his own off-field controversy is unclear.

Watson faced allegations of sexual misconduct and sexual assault from more than two dozen women, many of them massage therapists, stemming from encounters while he played for the Houston Texans. Although multiple women filed criminal complaints, two separate grand juries in Texas declined to indict him, and he was never charged with a crime. He has repeatedly denied wrongdoing, maintaining that any sexual activity was consensual.

In a 2022 deposition, Watson acknowledged sending an apologetic text message to Ashley Solis, the first woman to sue him, after she became tearful following a massage session in March 2020. “Sorry about you feeling uncomfortable. Never were the intentions,” Watson wrote, according to a transcript reported by USA Today.

Solis later told HBO’s Real Sports that she had felt threatened by comments Watson made about protecting their respective careers. She and another accuser, Kyla Hayes, also criticized the Browns’ decision to give Watson a fully guaranteed five-year, $230m contract after acquiring him from Houston in a blockbuster trade. “It’s just like a big screw you,” Solis said of the deal. Hayes said she felt Watson was “being rewarded for bad behavior”.

After the Texas grand juries declined to indict Watson on criminal complaints in 2022, the NFL subsequently suspended him for 11 games and fined him $5m for violating its personal conduct policy. Watson reached confidential settlements in most of the civil lawsuits against him.

Separately, Tucker faced allegations of sexually inappropriate conduct while a member of the Baltimore Ravens from 16 massage therapists who said incidents occurred between 2012 and 2016 at Baltimore-area spas. The allegations, first reported by the Baltimore Banner in January 2025, included claims that Tucker exposed himself, brushed therapists with his penis and left ejaculate on treatment tables. Two spas said they banned him from returning.

Tucker denied the allegations, with his lawyers describing them as “fictitious and utterly baseless”. Criminal charges were never brought against him. The Ravens subsequently released the seven-time Pro Bowl kicker in May 2025. After serving a 10-game NFL suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy, Tucker signed with Kansas City’s practice squad last month.

articles.headline: Experts warn: Nearly everyone in AI is susceptible to a honey-trap scheme right now
keyFacts: Former CIA officer Aaron Brown warned that tech founders and employees are vulnerable to honey-trap schemes aimed at stealing valuable AI secrets.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was accused of falling for a honey trap, and the WSJ reported OpenAI warned employees about outsiders seeking secrets.
Experts said AI makes generating fake personas easier, advising tech workers to recognize threats and separate personal and professional lives.
body: Even as the fall-out for Nvidia over Jensen Huang’s alleged honey-trap scandal is still unfolding, Silicon Valley has yet to reckon with a new reality: many more people among them are at risk.
“Nobody briefs founders on counterintelligence,” Aaron Brown, a former senior CIA officer and current founder of the software company Lumbra, told TechCrunch.

That’s because historically honey traps have been associated with politicians, the military, and national intelligence — the people “behind clearances and a workforce trained to expect an approach,” from spies and other attackers.

But now many of the most valuable secrets “sit inside companies building chips, models, and infrastructure,” Brown says, adding that a spy “wants what the CEO can touch. The roadmap, the export decisions, the customer list, who gets the technology. The CEO is the shortest path to all of it.”

Huang has been accused of falling for just such a honey trap by having an affair with Alice Huang. She’s a former executive of a Singapore neocloud who’s been accused of being a Chinese spy and of smuggling billions of dollars’ worth of restricted Nvidia chips into China.

After the Huang allegations broke, jokes flooded the internet about which tech CEO will be next, but it’s not just CEOs and founders who are at risk. The WSJ reported that OpenAI started warning its employees about outsiders trying to cozy up to them in search of company secrets. Anyone with access to sensitive information — from board members to executive assistants — can be the target of a honey trap.
And typically, the attackers aren’t lovers. Friendship is actually the oldest honey-trap scheme around, Brown said.

Honey traps gain access to their targets as investors, customers, recruiters, and consultancies. Their requests look legitimate on paper and don’t need their targets to fall in love. “They need you to feel comfortable talking,” Brown said. “They last longer because nobody’s looking.”

What’s interesting, too, is the irony. So many tech founders are moving to automate and digitize so much of human life and yet remain vulnerable to the oldest bug around, a person who preys on the human need to be understood by others.

“Why fight through a firewall when you can get close to the person who can open doors, influence decisions, or make requests nobody wants to question?” Perry Carpenter, a criminologist and chief deception strategist at KnowBe4, told TechCrunch.
Once targets realize they have been compromised, the threat can escalate: attackers now have a means of blackmail.

Another irony: AI has made honey-trapping much easier and cheaper. Planning a scheme used to take months or years of research, crafting a persona, knowing the target, and executing a plan. These days, it’s easy to use AI to research a target, generate fake social profiles, fake backgrounds, even fake voice calls.
“AI can help sustain an entire fictional backstory,” Carpenter said. “The technology helps set the stage, but the deception ultimately plays out through human relationships.”
The AI industry “became a national security industry faster than its culture caught up,” Brown said.
“Part of being honey-trapped is not knowing,” he added. “It doesn’t feel like manipulation. It feels genuine, even lucky.”

Carpenter said a good first step is looking for unusual patterns. Note, for instance, “coincidental encounters that happen a little too often,” he said. There are also obvious signs, like persistent curiosity about work and colleagues, or requesting secrecy about meeting up, and pressing for introductions or information.

Bigger red flags include if someone’s requests are getting bigger, pushing the boundaries of what you usually would be uncomfortable doing. “A simple gut check,” Brown said. “Would this person still be around if you lost your job tomorrow?”

It also helps to try and understand when emotions might be influencing a decision. Carpenter suggests putting up a clear boundary between one’s personal and professional life. Within companies, it also helps to “eliminate executive exceptionalism,” he said, the idea that the rules don’t apply to people in power at the company.

Brown added that company culture plays another role, too: Are employees comfortable with raising concerns, challenging unusual requests, and escalating possible threats? “One of the most dangerous security cultures is one where nobody feels comfortable questioning the CEO,” Carpenter said.
“Founders need to take risks, and they need to explore business opportunities,” Brown said. “Paranoia doesn’t help. Recognizing you’re a target does.”

articles.headline: YouTube is reportedly preparing to settle social media addiction claims for $3 billion
keyFacts: According to Bloomberg, YouTube reached an agreement in principle to pay $3 billion to school districts over addiction claims.
The settlement would allow Google to avoid lawsuits accusing social media platforms of negatively impacting teen mental health.
Bloomberg reported that the deal would also require YouTube to introduce new safeguards for teens.
body: YouTube is preparing to pay $3 billion to thousands of school districts to settle claims that its “addictive design” harmed kids, according to Bloomberg. Sources tell the publication that YouTube reached the agreement “in principle,” and that the deal would also include new safeguards for teens.
YouTube is reportedly preparing to settle social media addiction claims for $3 billion
The potential settlement would also require YouTube to introduce new safeguards for teens, Bloomberg reports.

The settlement would allow Google to avoid a wave of lawsuits filed by US school districts that accuse YouTube, Meta, Snap, and TikTok of negatively impacting the mental health of teen users. The first “bellwether” trial of these federal multidistrict litigation (MDL) cases was supposed to start in Kentucky in June, but all four companies settled for a total of $27 million before it went to court. The next trial is set for February 2027 before an Oakland, California, judge, with Meta, Snap, and TikTok as defendants.
Google didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

In August, Meta agreed to pay $17.1 billion over 10 years to settle lawsuits filed by a group of 47 states, along with several districts and territories. It also agreed to implement stricter safeguards for teens, but is pushing TikTok and YouTube to do the same. As part of the agreement, Meta will only shell out the remaining $5.3 billion of its $17.1 billion settlement if YouTube and TikTok roll out similar changes and pay matching amounts. In March, both YouTube and Meta were found negligent in a separate legal battle over social media addiction.

articles.headline: GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-sale copies and a bonkers $3.79 billion in its first day
keyFacts: Rockstar Games confirmed that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million pre-release copies for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.
Rockstar Games stated that GTA 6 earned $3.79 billion on its first day of worldwide release on November 19.
Rockstar co-founder Sam Houser expressed gratitude and excitement regarding the global player response.
body: Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.

Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November. By the end of its first day on sale, GTA 6 managed to rake in a frankly absurd $3.79bn. Not a bad haul.
As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a new record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history."

For context, GTA 5 made around $800m in its opening 24 hours more than a decade ago. That mammoth debut almost looks quaint next to GTA 6's stunning numbers, although it's notable GTA 5 didn't launch immediately in Japan or Brazil - GTA 6 is available in almost every market with access to PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," said Rockstar co-founder and company president, Sam Houser, in a recent press release. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you."

Previous estimates guessed that GTA 6 had sold almost 25m copies ($2.5bn in revenue) on day one. It's fair to say the game's staggering performance blew even those sky-high projections out of the water.

Every early indicator pointed to GTA 6's inevitably record-breaking launch. Parent company Take-Two previously said the game was tracking "well above expectations," as the crime fest sold more pre-orders than any other game in PlayStation Store and Xbox Store history.

The only question now is whether GTA 6 can ever outsell GTA 5's mammoth 230m copies, which it reached thanks to a very healthy cadence of GTA Online updates. How high GTA 6 can go will likely depend on its multiplayer offering, though Rockstar hasn't said anything concrete about that just yet.

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," Chris Tapsell gushed in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.
